passages.context: Articles 65 to 69 were read. Article 65 states that the Order of Readings for Sundays and the solemnities of the Lord extends over three years and for weekdays over two, each running independently of the other. Article 66 gives three readings on Sundays and solemnities of the Lord, Old Testament, apostle and gospel, notes that the three-year cycle means the same texts are read only every fourth year, and names harmony and semicontinuous reading as the governing principles. Article 67 explains that in Ordinary Time the apostolic and gospel readings are semicontinuous while the Old Testament reading is harmonised with the gospel. Article 68 declines to impose an organic harmony of themes on Sundays. Article 69 gives two readings on weekdays, an annual gospel cycle in Ordinary Time and a two-year first-reading cycle, Year I in odd and Year II in even years.

passages.context: Articles 74 to 77 were read. Article 74 reserves certain books to certain seasons, retaining the reading of Acts in Eastertide and of John in the later weeks of Lent and in Eastertide, and Isaiah in Advent. Article 75 states the criterion of length and the provision of longer and shorter forms. Article 76 states that in readings for Sundays and solemnities texts presenting real difficulties are avoided for pastoral reasons, while disallowing difficulty arising from inadequate religious education or inadequate biblical formation of pastors as a ground for omission. Article 77 states that the omission of verses has at times been the practice in many liturgical traditions including the Roman, that such omissions may not be made lightly for fear of distorting the meaning or the intent and style of Scripture, and that it was nevertheless decided on pastoral grounds to continue the practice while keeping the essential meaning intact.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The postconciliar Roman Rite book of readings for Mass, first published in 1969 and issued in a second Latin typical edition in 1981, distinct from the Missal in which the prayers and antiphons are printed. Its Praenotanda state the principles governing the selection and arrangement of the readings, including the three-year Sunday cycle, the two-year weekday first-reading cycle, and the criteria of length, difficulty and omission.
work.title: Ordo lectionum Missae
